what_its_for: This medicine helps control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It combines two medicines that work in different ways to lower your blood sugar. Pioglitazone helps your body use insulin better, and metformin lowers the amount of sugar your liver makes and helps your body respond to insulin more effectively. This medicine is used along with diet and exercise to manage your blood sugar.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with meals to help reduce stomach upset. Swallow the extended-release (XR) tablets whole — do not crush, cut, or chew them. Take the regular tablets with your largest meal of the day. If you take it once a day, take it at the same time every day. If you take it twice a day, take one dose in the morning and one in the evening with meals. Keep taking this medicine even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
dosing: Your doctor will choose the right dose for you based on your blood sugar levels and how well you tolerate the medicine. Common starting doses range from pioglitazone 15 mg to 30 mg combined with metformin 500 mg to 1000 mg per day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking too much alcohol while taking this medicine because it can lower your blood sugar too much and raise the risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis. Avoid skipping meals, as this can cause low blood sugar. Tell your doctor before having any X-ray or scan that uses contrast dye, because you may need to temporarily stop this medicine. Avoid starting new medicines, supplements, or herbal products without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you have: muscle pain, weakness, or cramps; trouble breathing; stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; feeling very cold; dizziness or feeling faint; unusual tiredness; signs of low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, fast heartbeat, or confusion; signs of heart failure such as sudden weight gain, swelling in your legs or ankles, or shortness of breath; vision changes or eye problems; dark-colored urine or yellowing of your skin or eyes; or any signs of a bladder infection like pain when you urinate or blood in your urine.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away, but it may take several weeks to see the full effect on your blood sugar. Most people notice better blood sugar control within 2 to 3 months. Keep taking your medicine and checking your blood sugar as your doctor recommends, even if you feel fine. Diet and exercise are also very important for managing your diabetes.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution because older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of metformin and have a higher risk of kidney problems. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Kidney problems: This medicine should NOT be used if your kidneys are not working well because it can raise the risk of a serious condition called lactic acidosis. Your doctor will do blood tests to check your kidney function. Liver problems: Do not use this medicine if you have liver problems. Heart failure: Pioglitazone can cause fluid retention and may worsen heart failure. Tell your doctor if you have any heart condition. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is not recommended during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor about safer options if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): Pioglitazone may increase the chance of getting pregnant. Use birth control if you do not want to become pregnant.
